acquisition_method.evidence: Mass spectra were acquired in a data-dependent manner, with an automatic switch between MS and MS/MS scans using a top 10 method.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: The search included variable modifications of methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation, and fixed modification of carbamidomethyl cysteine.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Cell lysates (100 μg) were diluted in 8 m urea in 0.1 m Tris-HCl followed by protein digestion with trypsin according to the FASP protocol.

fractionation_method.evidence: From each sample 40 μg of peptides were separated into six fractions by strong anion exchange as described previously.

fragmentation_method.evidence: Peptide fragmentation was performed with the HCD method and MS/MS spectra were acquired in the Orbitrap analyzer and a target value of 40,000 ions.

instrument.evidence: The high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was coupled to an LTQ-Orbitrap Velos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

ionization_type.evidence: inferred: Peptides were separated by reverse-phase chromatography on in-house made 20-cm columns (inner diameter 75 μm, 1.8 μm ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ media), using a nano-flow HPLC (Easy nanoLC, Thermo Fisher Scientific).

labeling.evidence: For SILAC experiments Jurkat, HEK293, LnCap, HeLa, and K562 cells were cultured in medium containing Lys8 and Arg10 instead of the natural amino acids, and supplemented with 10% dialyzed serum.
For comparison between samples we used label-free quantification with a minimum of two ratio counts to determine the normalized protein intensity.
